title: GPU state, memory pools and batching
summary: Understand how state buffers, geometry allocation and batching turn many entities into efficient draws.

blocks.text: State packs Transform, Paint and Material into typed-array-backed storage. GlobalStateAllocator reserves retained slots, recycles released slots and uploads changed ranges. Render commands refer to a state index rather than rebinding a uniform group for every entity. The state block’s byte size is computed from its components; verify State.size and the matching shader struct when changing fields.
Changing a CPU structure without changing WGSL alignment corrupts downstream fields. Padding, float/u32 reinterpretation and binding alignment are correctness requirements, not only optimizations.

GlobalGeometryAllocator suballocates shared vertex/index ranges; GlobalAnalyticalAllocator owns curve/contour data for analytical paths. Free-list reuse, capacity growth and binding rebuilds preserve valid offsets. MegaDrawBatchManager groups compatible path packets and uses programmable vertex pulling to reduce draw calls.

Batching depends on pipeline, textures, scissor/mask state and other compatible draw properties. A scene with many entities does not necessarily become a single draw call. Destroying an entity should release its retained ranges without destroying a buffer still shared by other entities.

Bit 31 selects mega-instance mode and bit 30 indicates the secondary/stroke pass. packInstanceIndex and WGSL getStateIndex/getLocalIndex must agree. Masks truncate overflowing indices, so these are representable limits rather than automatic safety checks. The GPU adds each draw’s local instance index to firstInstance; keep it within the selected mode’s range.

Some model/raymarch fragment paths receive material fields through flat varyings from the vertex stage. That avoids repeated per-fragment storage reads for those fields. It does not mean every shader is bindless or that no fragment shader ever reads a buffer. Varying layout and interpolation qualifiers must match the linked vertex and fragment stages.
One base circle and a compact transform array make shared instanced geometry visible.
